title: Ratios: The Cosmic Fuel Lab
subtitle: Ratios · Mission 02
tagline: Mix {{cyan:Cosmic Juice}} and {{magenta:Nebula Soda}} — and prove you can scale a recipe without breaking it.

slides.headline: The fleet needs {{cyan:Cosmic Fuel}} — and the mix has to be perfect.
body: Cosmic Fuel is a two-ingredient recipe. Each level uses a different pair of ingredients, but the math stays the same: it's all about the *ratio* between them.
Your job: get on the ingredient console and mix real batches. First a standard batch. Then an inversion test. Then scale it up — without breaking the recipe.
Three lab challenges. Three color pairs. The chamber tells you what's happening. Continue unlocks when your mix is right.

prompt.label: LEVEL 1 · STANDARD BATCH
prompt.question: Mix a standard batch of {{cyan:Cosmic Fuel}}: {{cyan:2 cups of juice}} for every {{magenta:1 cup of soda}}. Add ingredients until the chamber locks in a `2 : 1` ratio.

correct.title: ✓ FUEL CERTIFIED
body: That's the standard mix: **2 cups juice, 1 cup soda**. Twice as much juice as soda. The comparison — the *ratio* — is what makes this fuel work.
correct.followup: The word `ratio` just means "the comparison between two quantities." You wrote yours as `2 : 1`.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ KEEP MIXING
body: Not there yet. Check the telemetry panel — your current ratio has to match the target ratio.

config.instruction: Target ratio is 2 : 1. Add 2 cups of Cosmic Juice and 1 cup of Solar Soda to lock in.
config.hint: Add 2 cups of Cosmic Juice (cyan +) and 1 cup of Solar Soda (orange +). Twice as much juice as soda.

prompt.label: LEVEL 2 · INVERSION TEST
prompt.question: Now flip it. Mix {{magenta:2 cups of soda}} for every {{cyan:1 cup of juice}} — a `1 : 2` ratio. Same ingredients, different comparison.

correct.title: ✓ INVERSION LOGGED
body: Notice: `1 : 2` is a **totally different fuel** than `2 : 1`. Same ingredients, same total volume — but the *comparison* flipped. That's why order matters in a ratio.
This is the whole reason we write `2 : 1` instead of just `3` (the total): the ratio carries information the total can't.
correct.followup: In `A : B`, the first number always refers to the first thing named. `juice : soda = 1 : 2` means "1 juice for every 2 soda" — read it left to right.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ CHECK THE ORDER
body: This one asks for MORE soda than juice. If your juice number is bigger than your soda number, you've still got the old recipe.

config.instruction: Target ratio is 1 : 2. Void Juice on the low side, Plasma Soda on the high side.
config.hint: You want MORE soda than juice this time. Try 1 cup of Void Juice and 2 cups of Plasma Soda — or 2 cups of juice and 4 cups of soda, since 2 : 4 = 1 : 2.

prompt.label: LEVEL 3 · SCALE THE RECIPE
prompt.question: The fleet needs a bigger batch. Keep the original `2 : 1` ratio — but produce {{magenta:exactly 6 cups}} of Cosmic Fuel this time.

correct.title: ✓ HYPER-DRIVE FUELED
body: **4 cups juice, 2 cups soda.** Total = 6. Ratio = `4 : 2`, which simplifies back to `2 : 1` — same recipe, triple batch.
That's the trick with `equivalent ratios`: multiply *both sides* by the same number and the comparison doesn't change. `2 : 1` × 2 = `4 : 2`. The fuel tastes the same, there's just more of it.
correct.followup: This is exactly how a `unit rate` works in reverse. `2 : 1` is already a unit rate ("2 juice per 1 soda"). Any equivalent ratio — `4 : 2`, `6 : 3`, `20 : 10` — hides that same unit rate inside it.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ RIGHT RATIO, WRONG TOTAL
body: The ratio might be right, but the fleet needs **exactly 6 cups total**. Check the dashed TARGET line on the beaker — your fluid has to reach it exactly, still at a 2 : 1 mix.

config.instruction: Target ratio is 2 : 1, and total volume must be exactly 6 cups. Scale up without breaking the recipe.
config.hint: You need 6 cups total, split 2 : 1. That means 2 parts Warp Juice + 1 part Fuel Soda = 3 parts total. Each part = 6 ÷ 3 = 2 cups. So: 4 cups of Warp Juice and 2 cups of Fuel Soda.

slides.headline: LAB CERTIFIED
slides.subtext: You mixed the standard batch, proved that order matters, and scaled the recipe without breaking it. That's ratios, cadet.
